text:
been LPing on @MeteoraAG DLMM for a while now.

from today, 1 post a day on what actually works:
- how bins + shapes work
- safety checks before every pool
- when to exit
- real wins and real losses

follow if you LP or want to start

DLMM in one tweet:

instead of spreading liquidity across every price, it splits price into bins.

you pick which bins hold your liquidity. only bins that price trades through earn fees.

tighter range = more fees per $
but price leaves your range faster

volume is not safety.

a pool can do $5M volume and still be:
- bundled supply
- wash traded
- one dev wallet away from zero

volume tells you fees are possible. it tells you nothing about whether the token survives the day

bin step = the price gap between bins, in basis points.

100 bps = 1%

small bin step: tight spacing, better for calmer pairs
big bin step: wide spacing, survives volatility

matching bin step to how much the token moves is half the game

the LP formula nobody tweets:

net = fees + price change - divergent loss - costs

green fees is not a green position.

if price dumps through your range you end up holding the token that dumped. fees have to outrun that

3 DLMM shapes, 3 different bets:

spot: liquidity spread evenly. works in most conditions
curve: stacked in the middle. best when price stays calm
bid-ask: stacked at the edges. catches big swings, DCA in/out

pick the shape from your thesis, not from someone's screenshot

rule #1 before any meteora pool:

copy the CA from a trusted source. never search by ticker.

there are always 5 tokens with the same name. the fake one usually has the most "volume"

same token, different pools, different risk.

before depositing check the exact pool:
- bin step
- base fee
- liquidity
- LP lock for THAT pool

"LP locked" on a token page can be talking about a different pool

mint + freeze authority revoked?

good. still not safe.

it removes 2 ways the dev can hurt you. it doesn't stop:
- insiders dumping
- bundled wallets
- the narrative dying

checklists reduce risk. none of them remove it

part of my DLMM book is now copy-LP through Valhalla.

I pick wallets with a long closed-position history, not one lucky week. it opens and closes for me, I still review what it enters.

reply "ref" if you want to try it

your position went out of range. now what?

not panic. options:
- hold and wait for price to come back
- withdraw and re-enter around the new price
- zap out to SOL
- close and move on

which one depends on one thing: is your thesis still true?

60 seconds on bubblemaps before every LP.

looking for:
- clusters of wallets funded from the same source
- top holders linked to the dev
- big bubbles that aren't the LP pool

if the map looks like a spiderweb, you're the exit liquidity

a 5% fee pool is not 5x better than a 1% fee pool.

high fees usually exist because the token is extremely volatile.

the question isn't "how high is the fee"
it's "will real flow pay me more than the inventory I'll lose"

before I open any position I write down 5 things:

1. why this pool
2. size
3. range + shape
4. what makes me close
5. max loss

takes 2 minutes. saves me from every emotional exit

small meteora detail most new LPs miss:

creating a new pool or bin arrays = rent you don't get back
opening a position = rent you DO get back when you close it

closing old dust positions isn't pointless. you're reclaiming SOL

spotting fake volume in 3 checks:

1. volume is insanely high vs the liquidity
2. very few unique traders
3. huge volume but price barely moves

real flow is messy. fake flow is suspiciously smooth

check the pool price vs jupiter before depositing.

if the meteora pool is priced off from the rest of the market, arb bots will fix it through your liquidity.

and you'll be the cheap side of that trade

the best LPs I know try to kill the trade before they take it.

they look for reasons NOT to enter first.

if the pool survives that, they size small.

process > prediction

why your PnL card says one thing and your wallet says another:

some tools show PnL in USD. if SOL moved while you were in, the USD number moved too, even if your SOL result didn't.

always know which unit you're measuring in

LPs: what's your default shape for fresh memecoin pools?

spot / curve / bid-ask

and what bin step?

curious what's actually working for people right now

meteora LPs earned ~$140M in fees in H1 2026 on ~$32B of volume.

~75% of those fees came from tokens NOT launched on meteora.

LP isn't just a memecoin side quest. it's where solana's trading volume pays out

one-sided SOL bid-ask under a token = DCA-ing into it as it drops, and earning fees while you do.

the catch: if it keeps dropping, you end up 100% in the token.

only run it on tokens you'd actually be ok holding

testing a new LP strategy? size it like you expect it to fail.

- small first position
- wider downside range
- write down what happened

scale only after it works more than once

what I check before copying a wallet's LP on Valhalla:

- 50+ closed positions, not 5
- consistent wins, not one 10x
- sizing that doesn't blow up on one rug
- still active this week

copying is easy. picking who to copy is the skill. reply "ref" for my link

"fees are green so I'll hold"

most expensive sentence in LP.

fees can be +20% while the position is -40% because the token dumped through your range.

look at net, not fees

meteora tip: zap out has a bin limit.

if your position is very wide, zap out may not work in one go. withdraw normally, then swap on jupiter.

know this before you need it, not mid-dump

my LP stack, all free:

dexscreener: find flow
gmgn: holders + dev
bubblemaps: wallet clusters
rugcheck: authorities
jupiter: price check
meteora: enter + manage
metlex: PnL cards

no tool tells you "safe". each one answers one question

close or reassess when:
- price leaves your range
- fee flow dies
- volume starts looking fake
- pool price drifts from the market
- your reason for entering isn't true anymore

"it might come back" is not on the list

DLMM vs DAMM v2 on meteora:

DLMM: bins, you choose range + shape. more control, more babysitting
DAMM v2: simpler AMM, configurable fee schedules, NFT positions

watching charts all day? DLMM
want less management? look at DAMM v2

my rules for posting PnL here:

- I'll show losers too, not just green cards
- tx so you can verify
- the setup, not just the number

if someone only ever posts wins, ask what they're not showing you
